findings.evidence: Before delegating any step, ask: what does a subagent give here that the main thread lacks: isolation from a large search, a specialized registered agent, or parallel work? If none, run it directly.
findings.fix: Shorten this to the parts specific to commands: 'Delegate only with an agent type that exists (built-ins: Explore, Plan, general-purpose) or with context: fork plus agent:, and honor "no agents".' Drop the generic when-to-delegate reasoning, which the model and harness already handle.

findings.evidence: The Process workflow (## Workflow) is followed by Tool-style reference tables (## Location, ## Patterns, ## Frontmatter, ## Arguments and pre-run context), so the phased checkpoints and the lookup material are interleaved
findings.fix: Mark each table as the lookup for its workflow step (for example 'Step 3 lookup' over ## Location and 'Step 5 lookup' over ## Frontmatter), so the Process pattern stays the spine and the tables read as its reference.

findings.evidence: Six evals cover iterative fixing, simple execution, a side-effect workflow, arguments that are special to the shell and a name collision, but none covers the Plan, approve, execute pattern or the approved-update path (step 2 option 2)
findings.fix: Add an eval that asks for a plan-then-implement command, with assertions that it writes nothing before an explicit approval signal and that it names where the plan is saved. Add a second eval in which the user approves updating an existing command, with assertions that it reads the file first, keeps the frontmatter and shows a diff.

findings.evidence: If the workflow needs bundled scripts or reference files, say a skill fits better (out of scope here).
findings.fix: Give this branch an outcome: 'say a skill fits better and stop without writing; if the user still wants a command, write one that calls the existing scripts by path and flag each missing script as a manual step.' Also note that the agent cannot see the / menu (line 41), so it should tell the user to check for /name instead of claiming it checked.

findings.evidence: The submit-stack example takes `$ARGUMENTS` as the basis for the commit message, then shows `git commit -m "[Single sentence summary of what was done]"`. Double-quoted shell text still expands dollar expressions and command substitutions, contradicting SKILL.md's required single-quoted encoding for argument-derived values.
findings.fix: Add an explicit encoding step for the final commit message: encode it as one single-quoted shell word, escaping embedded single quotes, then run `git commit -m <encoded-message>`. Update the example snippet accordingly and preserve its upstream attribution.

findings.evidence: The checklist requires an approved update to have 'no other skill or command shares the name (if one does, stop and use the step 2 template)'. When both a same-named skill and command exist, as in the collision fixture, approving either offered update returns to the same collision menu rather than completing the update.
findings.fix: Make the initial collision offer distinguish viable resolutions: a renamed command, an explicitly approved resolution of the shadowing collision before updating the command, or routing a requested SKILL.md edit out of scope. Carry the selected resolution into the approved-update checklist instead of returning to the unchanged menu.

findings.evidence: 'The frontmatter is read only when `---` is on line 1; broken YAML loads the body with no fields and no error' repeats the same loading constraint stated again in Gotchas at line 92.
findings.fix: Keep the complete silent-frontmatter warning and its auto-invocation consequence once in Gotchas; replace the repeated explanation in Frontmatter with a short cross-reference.
